method_notes: All analytical content in this dataset is ASSESSMENT-level open-source staff work pending Defence custodian validation; no record asserts partner intent, treaty status or dates beyond the cited evidence register records.
Scores are ordinal decision aids (V7 s49). Partner-option scores exist only per opportunity; no universal best-partner score is generated (V7 s13 hard rule).

Scoring: each criterion 0-5 against anchored scales; weighted points = weight x (score/5). Unknown scores are excluded from the weighted sum and contribute no points; the headline partner-option score is the raw weighted sum on the full 100-point weight set (scoring-and-comparison-rules.md s1 - renormalisation is not an authorised method). Where Unknowns exist, a renormalised value (x100/known-weight) is declared in score_arithmetic as a sensitivity view only and never carries the headline score or band (red-team adjudication 2026-07-18; previously renormalised values were the headline for OPP-02 P-DE, OPP-07, OPP-11, OPP-13, OPP-15 P-US). Confidence caps (scoring-and-comparison-rules.md s5): any Unknown on a >=15-weight criterion or >=3 Unknowns caps evidence_confidence at Low; any other Unknown caps it at Medium.
Opportunity score, pathway status and evidence confidence are stored and displayed separately and are never merged (V7 s25, s70).

Pathway overall status per V7 s50: any BLACK -> BLACK; else any RED -> RED; else any AMBER or UNKNOWN -> AMBER; else GREEN. NOT_APPLICABLE components are excluded. Every option names its binding gap (s60).

Treatment matrix operationalisation (V7 s13.1): Act now = A/B value with Green pathway, or activity already in execution or a live window closing within ~12 months (noted in rationale); Build pathway = A/B value with an Amber/Red binding gap; Quick win = B/C value with Green pathway and low resource demand; Explore = C-band or validation-dependent options; Hold = weak value or Red/Black without a near-term lever.

Acceptance-test cases present: in OPP-08 the highest-scoring option (P-US, 72/B) carries a RED pathway on the security component (MTCR launch-vehicle exclusions from the AUKUS exemption, EV-AUKUSLFE-05); OPP-13 carries a RED instrument component (EV-UAE-21).

Where the register verification verdict is CORRECTED the corrected wording is used, e.g. CSpO Vision 2031 released 22 Feb 2022 US time (EV-RONINS20-03) and the Quad Satellite Data Portal as a link gateway, not a centralised data platform (EV-QUADINDI-02).
Evidence shortfalls and TO_VERIFY dependencies are recorded in confidence_note fields and levered through the gaps_levers backlog; all gap owners are TO_ASSIGN pending validation.

partners.name: Canada

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored 3/5 on space-specificity against the anchors (US=5, Japan=4, Germany=2, NZ=2). Canada clears the Germany/NZ bar of 2 because bilateral space instruments actually exist: DFAT lists 'space cooperation' among the Australia-Canada bilateral agreements (EV-CANADA-09) and a CSA-ASA MoU was updated in April 2024 (EV-CANADA-13) — where Germany's rationale for 2 was precisely the absence of any bilateral G2G space instrument. Canada also shares with Australia the same operational US SATCOM programme (WGS, EV-CANADA-11), the same US-SSN sensor-contributor role (Sapphire, EV-CANADA-04), CSpO co-membership including Vision 2031 joint release (EV-CANADA-07), and a live G2G materiel arrangement with a joint R&D framework (A-OTHR, EV-CANADA-08). It does not reach Japan's 4 because every defence-space channel is multilateral or US-mediated: no Australia-Canada defence-space instrument, dialogue or data-sharing arrangement was identified (EV-CANADA-18), the known bilateral space layer is civil and of unverified depth (EV-CANADA-13 scope unknown), and space is not named at leaders' level (EV-CANADA-09). Not inflated for general warmth: the alliance-dense general relationship and the radar export are adjacent evidence, not space evidence.

partners.one_line: Canada is Australia's structural twin in allied defence space — same US-SSN sensor role, same WGS programme, same CSpO founding cohort, new multi-billion space funding — with a civil-only bilateral space layer and no bilateral defence-space instrument, one instrument-extension away from one via the June 2026 A-OTHR joint R&D framework.

partners.name: France

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored above Germany (anchor 2) and below Japan (anchor 4), on space specificity rather than general warmth. Germany's 2 reflects CSpO co-membership and strong capability with no bilateral government-to-government space instrument; France clears that bar three times over: a ministerial Declaration of Intent on military space cooperation naming earth observation, SSA and milsatcom (EV-FRANCE-10), an ASA-CNES MoU published 30 April 2024 (EV-FRANCE-12), and a leaders-endorsed roadmap with a standing space-cooperation chapter including an explicit SSA commitment (EV-FRANCE-11) — on top of shared CSpO membership (EV-FRANCE-08) and, since 14 October 2024, shared MNF-OOD membership (EV-FRANCE-09). It stays below 4 because nothing beyond declared intent is evidenced: no operational data exchange, no combined space exercising, no liaison presence, no binding instrument; the entire space architecture is 2022-2024 vintage built during the post-AUKUS repair (EV-FRANCE-13, EV-FRANCE-14), and one round of collection found no implementation evidence under either space instrument. Intent-rich, operations-poor: 3/5, not scored higher precisely to avoid rewarding paper over practice.

partners.one_line: France pairs Europe's most complete military-space capability and Pacific residency with a young, post-AUKUS-repair bilateral space architecture — a military-space Declaration of Intent, an ASA-CNES MoU and a roadmap space chapter — none of it yet evidenced as operationalised.

partners.name: Italy

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored level with Germany (2) and New Zealand (2), on space specificity. The Germany-2 condition — CSpO co-member, genuinely capable, but no bilateral government-to-government space instrument — holds for Italy almost exactly: CSpO member since December 2023 (EV-USSFCSPO-08), a full sovereign military space stack (EV-ITALY-07 to EV-ITALY-12), but the only bilateral instrument is a narrow agency-level statement of intent of 17 February 2020 'to consider' one ISS activity, with no evidenced follow-through (EV-ITALY-03, EV-ITALY-04). Italy arguably edges Germany on paper because its agency instrument is confirmed against the primary text where Germany's 2019 DLR letter remains TO_VERIFY, and DFAT declares a 'strong partnership' (EV-ITALY-02) — but declaratory warmth does not move the score, exactly as New Zealand's alliance-grade general relationship did not. Well short of Japan (4): no G2G space agreement, no defence-space instrument, no operational space cooperation, and a general defence relationship that produced its first exercise participation only in 2024 (EV-ITALY-17). Not a 1: the CSpO seat, the live instrument, founding co-signature of the Artemis Accords (EV-ITALY-13) and parallel DA-ASAT commitments (EV-ITALY-14) are real space-specific fabric. One-round baseline — score provisional pending a second round.

partners.one_line: Italy is the inverse New Zealand: a full-stack military space power (sovereign SAR, milsatcom, optical ISR, a 2020 space command, a 2025 national space law, CSpO from December 2023) whose entire bilateral space channel with Australia is one dormant 2020 agency statement of intent.

partners.name: Norway

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored level with Germany (2) and New Zealand (2) on space specificity, not relationship warmth. Norway meets the Germany-anchor formula exactly: CSpO co-member (from December 2023, EV-NORWAY-04), genuinely capable in niche space lanes (ASBM HEO SATCOM with allied hosted payloads, EV-NORWAY-07/-08; world-leading polar ground segment, EV-NORWAY-11; sovereign orbital launch site, EV-NORWAY-13), but no bilateral government-to-government space instrument with Australia of any kind (EV-NORWAY-02). Two features pull in opposite directions and net out: the space-specific Australia track is even emptier than Germany's (no project-level touchpoints equivalent to DLR-TeraNet or Koonibba launches — nothing at all), while the materiel-industrial relationship is thicker than any other maturity-2 partner's (up to $850m Williamtown factory, GWEO strategic partnership, $142m JSM contract, reciprocal 2024 ministerial visits — EV-NORWAY-03/-16/-17) and Norway hosts CSpO senior officials in Oslo in December 2026 (EV-NORWAY-05). Not a 1: the shared CSpO seat plus real capability plus a warm ministerial channel exceed a bare-acquaintance score. Nowhere near Japan (4): no bilateral space instrument, no operational integration (not even MNF-OOD membership, EV-NORWAY-06), no space dialogue. One-round scoring; not to be ranked against two-round partners without a second round.

partners.one_line: Capable niche space nation and Australia's fastest-growing missile-industrial partner — with a completely empty bilateral space rail; CSpO is the only shared space vehicle, and Oslo hosts its senior officials in December 2026.

partners.name: Republic of Korea

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored 3/5 on space specificity against the anchors (US=5, Japan=4, Germany=2, NZ=2). The ROK clears the bar that caps Germany and New Zealand at 2: a dedicated bilateral government-to-government space instrument exists — the December 2021 MoU on Space Cooperation for Peaceful Purposes with a standing annual Space Policy Dialogue (EV-ROK-02) — refreshed at agency level by the October 2025 KASA-ASA MoU and Statement of Intent (EV-ROK-03), and the 2015 defence Blueprint carries an explicit 'cooperate on space security' commitment (EV-ROK-04). It does not reach Japan's 4 because the defence-space lane is empty in practice: the ROK is not a CSpO member (EV-ROK-18), shares no operational or exercise-level space channel with Australia (EV-ROK-05), its allied military-space integration runs through the US bilateral and US-Japan-ROK trilateral lanes (EV-ROK-10, EV-ROK-12), and the bilateral space track located is civil-led with no evidence of military space data flows, combined space operations or a defence-space instrument. One-round baseline; do not inflate further without verifying the Space Policy Dialogue's actual cadence since 2022.

partners.one_line: The inverse of the New Zealand finding: a partner with real bilateral space instruments (2021 Space MoU, annual Space Policy Dialogue, 2025 KASA-ASA MoU) and serious sovereign capability, but sitting outside CSpO — so Australia's defence-space architecture and the ROK's have no shared room to meet in.

partners.name: Singapore

relationship_maturity.rationale: Scored 1/5 on space-specificity, deliberately below Germany (2) and New Zealand (2). Both anchors hold CSpO membership - a standing, space-specific operational vehicle shared with Australia - and were scored 2 despite having no bilateral space instrument. Singapore has neither the bilateral instrument NOR any allied space structure: it is not in CSpO and not in Five Eyes (EV-SINGAPORE-15), no ASA-OSTIn or other agency MoU could be evidenced (EV-SINGAPORE-14, -15), and the word 'space' is absent from CSP 2.0, the DFAT country brief and the 2023/2024 SAJMC communiques (EV-SINGAPORE-03, -04, -05, -06). The only space-specific overlap is multilateral and thin: OST, COPUOS and the Artemis Accords (EV-SINGAPORE-13). Singapore's genuine sovereign capability (TeLEOS-1/-2, EV-SINGAPORE-10, -11) and the alliance-depth general defence relationship (EV-SINGAPORE-02, -07) do not raise the score, because the score measures the space partnership, not capability or warmth - the same discipline applied to New Zealand. Not scored 0 because the shared Artemis Accords/COPUOS/OST membership and a live bilateral defence S&T channel (EV-SINGAPORE-02, -06) give real, citable touchpoints a first space initiative could use. One-round baseline; score provisional pending items 1-3 of the validation backlog - an actual ASA-OSTIn MoU, if confirmed, would move Singapore to 2.

partners.one_line: Australia's deepest Southeast Asian defence partnership - treaty-level training presence, biennial 3+3, A$2.25bn of Singaporean capital in Queensland - has a bilateral space relationship of exactly zero, despite Singapore flying its own 1 m optical and SAR satellites in an equatorial niche no allied nation occupies.

partners.name: New Zealand

relationship_maturity.rationale: REVISED 3/5 at round-2 reconciliation (22 Jul 2026; originally 2). The prior score rested on 'no bilateral space instrument was located' (EV-NZ-17) - falsified by round 2: the MBIE-ASA Arrangement Regarding Space Cooperation for Peaceful Purposes (22 Oct 2019, non-binding, Joint Steering Committee, SSA listed) exists, plus MNF-OOD co-membership (from 5 Sep 2024), SouthPAN operational joint delivery and the Catalyst/Takahe programme to 2029. relationship_maturity.rationale: ADAPTED READING: for the internal partner the 0-5 scale is read as Defence's engagement maturity with its own space industrial and academic base (density, stability and instrumentation of the demand relationship), not alliance maturity. Scored 2: above 1 because standing, funded, space-specific instruments genuinely exist (SmartSat CRC since 2019, the $180m iLAuNCH Trailblazer, the DSTG Resilient Multi-Mission Space STaR Shot, the RAAF-UNSW Canberra M-series line, an operating ASA launch licensing regime) and an operational Space Command sits on the Defence side. Not 3, because the through-line a 3 would require is missing on the fetched record: the flagship JP9102 SATCOM procurement was cancelled on 4 November 2024 (confirmed), the largest R&D consortium's Commonwealth funding ended 30 June 2026 with its successor unconfirmed, the space-facing trailblazer sits under the education portfolio rather than Defence, ASCA shows no evidenced space mission, and no standing Defence-space industry partnership forum was located at all. The A$38bn/2036 investment line does not raise the score: announced money is not engagement.

partners.one_line: Every partnership in this model runs through a domestic base that Defence funds generously at the R&D layer but has never anchored with a stable, instrumented demand signal — the capability is real, the through-line is missing.

australian_inputs.title: Assured multi-orbit military SATCOM after JP9102 cancellation
australian_inputs.description: Defence ceased JP9102 procurement on 4 November 2024, stating a single-orbit GEO system would not meet strategic priorities; SPA9102 holds only First Pass approval with a narrowband-only RFI, while the ADF relies on US WGS access and hosted payloads on Optus C-1 and Intelsat IS-22.
australian_inputs.authority: Defence cancellation announcement 4 Nov 2024; 2024 IIP resilient SATCOM investment line
australian_inputs.success_condition: Multi-orbit SATCOM capability approved and contracted, with assured interim wideband and narrowband access maintained.

leverage_points.why: The 2007 WGS MoU carries Australia's assured wideband access - the interim backbone until a multi-orbit capability is approved; the evidenced access horizon is 2029.
leverage_points.next_action: Open negotiation of an extended assured-access annex before the 2029 WGS access horizon identified in round-2 reporting (EV-MILSATCO-22, EV-MILSATCO-15).

leverage_points.why: AUSMIN is the ministerial forum that has historically endorsed SATCOM cooperation steps; the ANZUS 75th anniversary falls September 2026 and AUSMIN 2025 flagged commemoration.
leverage_points.next_action: Table the wideband and alternative-communications lines of effort - the unscoped partnership decision space (EV-MILSATCO-10) - at the next AUSMIN. No 2026 AUSMIN is scheduled in evidence (last held 8 December 2025, VEH-US-02); the ANZUS 75th anniversary (September 2026, VEH-US-01) is an agenda hook, not a scheduled meeting.
leverage_points.timing: next AUSMIN (not yet scheduled as of 18 Jul 2026)

leverage_points.why: The June 2026 USSF-Australian Space Command Statement of Intent commits both services to deepen cooperation in military space operations, giving SATCOM resilience a service-chief channel.
leverage_points.next_action: Use the SoI channel to align allied augmentation options with the SPA9102 narrowband RFT before the AusTender close of 19 August 2026 (EV-MILSATCO-09, TO_VERIFY; EV-USSFFORC-12).

leverage_points.why: The Enhanced Space Cooperation force-posture initiative is the standing umbrella for US space capability cooperation on Australian territory.
leverage_points.next_action: Scope a project arrangement for multi-orbit interim services consistent with the 2026 IIP A$5.2-7.2bn SATCOM envelope (EV-MILSATCO-12).

australian_inputs.title: Layered space domain awareness (JP9360)
australian_inputs.description: JP9360 seeks a distributed, multi-technology capability for threat warning, attribution, detection, tracking and characterisation of space objects, building on the Exmouth C-band radar and Space Surveillance Telescope.
australian_inputs.authority: JP9360 tranche-based program; Defence Space Strategy 2022 ($2b SSA line to 2038)
australian_inputs.success_condition: Tranche deliveries provide Defence-usable threat warning and attribution across orbits.

leverage_points.why: DARC is the flagship trilateral deep-space sensing programme hosted at Exmouth; Site 1 is in Early Use with full operations expected 2027.
leverage_points.next_action: Confirm Australian data-access terms before full operations (expected 2027); Early Use has run since September 2025 by the US 20th Space Surveillance Squadron from Eglin (EV-SDAPROGR-08, EV-SDAPROGR-09).

leverage_points.why: The reported 1 May 2026 expanded space-surveillance partnership would integrate DARC, the SST and the upgraded C-band radar, with USSF intent to connect Australian sensors to the Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture by late 2026.
leverage_points.next_action: Verify the announcement (EV-SDAPROGR-13, TO_VERIFY) and, if confirmed, formalise the sensor-integration project arrangement on the reported late-2026 PWSA connection timeline.

leverage_points.why: AUKMIN June 2026 committed to SDA capability collaboration with the UK - the third DARC nation and Site 2 host (Cawdor Barracks, completion scheduled February 2030).
leverage_points.next_action: Convert the AUKMIN commitment (vehicle TO_VERIFY) into a defined UK-Australia SDA workplan aligned with DARC Site 2 delivery (EV-SDAPROGR-09).

leverage_points.why: The March 2026 Australia-Germany Declaration of Intent on a global space-surveillance sensor network adds non-US catalogue diversity to JP9360 outcomes.
leverage_points.next_action: Negotiate the implementing arrangement under the Declaration of Intent (in force March 2026) for reciprocal sensor-data exchange.

leverage_points.why: JCO provides a commercial-unclassified SDA layer that Australia already operates through the Adelaide Commercial Data Mission Centre.
leverage_points.next_action: Extend commercial SDA data contracts through the JCO construct, building on the September 2025 JCO-200 delivery (EV-JAPANSDA-16).

australian_inputs.title: Sustain allied SDA hosting while protecting sovereign SDA funding
australian_inputs.description: DARC hosting demonstrates Australia's southern-hemisphere value, but commentary reports DARC support costs create funding pressure on the sovereign JP9360 program - a tension requiring explicit management.
australian_inputs.authority: DARC trilateral MoU (announced 1-2 Dec 2023); JP9360 program
australian_inputs.success_condition: DARC Site 1 reaches full operations (expected 2027) without displacing JP9360 tranche funding.

leverage_points.why: DARC hosting is the largest single Australian SDA contribution and the strongest offset card - but support costs are reported to pressure sovereign JP9360 funding.
leverage_points.next_action: Set an explicit Defence position on DARC support costs versus JP9360 tranches before full operations expected 2027 (EV-SDAPROGR-09, EV-AUINPUTS-14).

leverage_points.why: The Space Surveillance Telescope reached Final Operational Capability on 19 August 2025 with an Australian-industry mirror recoat - proof the hosting model returns sovereign industrial value.
leverage_points.next_action: Lock post-FOC sustainment and Australian tasking shares under the SST relocation MoU (EV-SDAPROGR-10, EV-SDAPROGR-11).

leverage_points.why: The C-band radar - first Space Surveillance Network sensor in the Southern Hemisphere - completes the Exmouth triple that anchors Australia's value proposition.
leverage_points.next_action: Verify the reported 2026 C-band upgrade within the expanded surveillance partnership (EV-SDAPROGR-13, TO_VERIFY) and record it as an Australian offset.

leverage_points.why: AUSMIN is where hosting contributions can be explicitly counted as burden-sharing offsets in partnership negotiations.
leverage_points.next_action: Present the hosting-offset ledger (SST FOC, C-band FOC, DARC Early Use) at the next AUSMIN as a supporting burden-sharing argument, not a standalone ask (last AUSMIN held 8 December 2025; ANZUS 75th anniversary September 2026 is a hook, not a scheduled meeting).
leverage_points.timing: next AUSMIN (not yet scheduled as of 18 Jul 2026)

australian_inputs.title: Resilient PNT for the ADF in GNSS-degraded environments
australian_inputs.description: Defence established a Joint PNT Directorate in April 2024 and runs a Quantum-Assured PNT STaR Shot; nationally, Australia relies wholly on foreign-owned GNSS (GPS, QZSS and others) with no sovereign constellation.
australian_inputs.authority: Joint PNT Directorate (est. April 2024); DSTG STaR Shots
australian_inputs.success_condition: ADF maintains accurate PNT in the absence of GNSS signals; national augmentation resilience improved.

leverage_points.why: QZSS ground-segment hosting in Australia is the evidenced regional-augmentation channel; QZS-6/QZS-7 also host US SDA payloads, coupling the PNT and SDA agendas.
leverage_points.next_action: Verify the QZSS hosting arrangements (vehicle TO_VERIFY) and scope expanded monitoring/augmentation infrastructure once QZS-7 launches (postponed pending the H3 F8 investigation; rescheduled per JAXA release of 8 July 2026 - EV-JAPANSDA-15).

leverage_points.why: M-code access is the core allied military-PNT layer: the GPS III constellation completed 21 April 2026 and more than 100,000 M-code receivers are delivered, but Australia's MGUE Project Arrangement accession is unconfirmed.
leverage_points.next_action: Confirm or complete Australian accession to the December 2020 multinational MGUE Increment 1 Project Arrangement (Australia expressed intent in 2021 - EV-RESILIEN-09) at the next AUSMIN; if the ministerial slate is full, route via the USSF-Australian Space Command service-chief channel (VEH-US-25) instead.
leverage_points.timing: next AUSMIN or VEH-US-25 service-chief channel (no 2026 AUSMIN scheduled as of 18 Jul 2026)

leverage_points.why: The AUKUS licence-free environment carries the sovereign quantum-PNT line (QuantX optical clocks were contracted in 2024 expressly as enabling AUKUS partners' PNT development).
leverage_points.next_action: Structure the TEMPO.Space clock demonstration (frequency comb launched 30 March 2026 - EV-RESILIEN-14) as an AUKUS-tradeable deliverable (EV-RESILIEN-13).

leverage_points.why: TTCP is the standing five-nation S&T forum where assured-PNT research (JP9380, quantum clocks, NAVWAR test methods) can be burden-shared.
leverage_points.next_action: Table Joint PNT Directorate GPS-denial trial results from Talisman Sabre 2025 (EV-RESILIEN-06, EV-RESILIEN-07) into the TTCP programme.

australian_inputs.title: Earth observation service continuity without a sovereign EO mission
australian_inputs.description: NSMEO was cancelled in June 2023; EO satellites support over 170 Australian government programs, so continuity rests on foreign missions plus ground-segment investment (Alice Springs upgrade, Landsat Next partnership).
australian_inputs.authority: 2024-25 Budget ($207.4m GA EO Program); Landsat Next commitment (A$448.7m/11 years)
australian_inputs.success_condition: Assured, treaty- or arrangement-backed access to EO data streams for all critical programs.

leverage_points.why: The Landsat Next core partnership was signed at AUSMIN (5 August 2024); AUSMIN is where the US restructure must be addressed.
leverage_points.next_action: Seek clarified Landsat Next terms after the FY2026 US budget request funded no Landsat Next as designed and requirements were descoped to a single satellite (EV-EOCONTIN-08, EV-EOCONTIN-09) - no Australian public response is yet evidenced (EV-EOCONTIN-10). Raise at the next AUSMIN (last held 8 December 2025; no 2026 edition scheduled in evidence).
leverage_points.timing: next AUSMIN (not yet scheduled as of 18 Jul 2026)

leverage_points.why: GA has historically been JAXA's Oceania data-distribution node for ALOS, but no ALOS-4 access arrangement is evidenced - a concrete diversification gap the MoC can close.
leverage_points.next_action: Negotiate an ALOS-4 access arrangement (ALOS-4 launched July 2024; distribution proceeding via Japanese commercial providers - EV-EOCONTIN-15, TO_VERIFY).

leverage_points.why: Quad EO commitments (satellite data portal, capacity-building) give a civil diversification channel that costs little and hedges bilateral legs.
leverage_points.next_action: Keep EO data-sharing on the Quad space working group agenda through the next summit cycle (EV-QUADINDI-05).

leverage_points.why: The 2012 ISRO-ASA MoU (amended 17 February 2021) expressly covers Earth observation - an under-used diversification instrument.
leverage_points.next_action: Scope an EO data-access line under the amended MoU alongside the Gaganyaan cooperation (EV-INDIACOC-05).

australian_inputs.title: Assured weather-satellite services (Himawari dependency)
australian_inputs.description: BoM forecasts and warnings are critically dependent on JMA's Himawari; the November 2024 BoM-JMA strategic arrangement and Himawari-10 contribution are the primary mitigation, with no sovereign alternative before the early 2030s.
australian_inputs.authority: BoM-JMA strategic relationship arrangement (11 Nov 2024); BoM CEO statement
australian_inputs.success_condition: Continuity of high-cadence weather imagery contractually assured through Himawari-10.

leverage_points.why: The 2+2 is the ministerial channel above the BoM-JMA Strategic Relationship Arrangement of 11 November 2024 that governs the Himawari dependency (the SRA itself is not yet a vehicle-register record - evidence shortfall).
leverage_points.next_action: Elevate Himawari-10 continuity - development delayed per round-2 assessment (EV-EOCONTIN-14, EV-EOCONTIN-21) - to the next 2+2 agenda (12th held 5 September 2025).

leverage_points.why: The JAXA-ASA Memorandum of Cooperation is the standing civil-space instrument that can carry contingency imagery and data arrangements adjacent to the JMA line.
leverage_points.next_action: Scope a contingency-access annex covering interruption of JMA services at comparable cadence (success condition of this input; EV-CONVERSA-03).

leverage_points.why: Annual Leaders' Meetings have carried the bilateral space agenda at head-of-government level and can lock in Himawari-10 co-investment visibility.
leverage_points.next_action: Reference the Himawari-10 co-investment - Australia's largest meteorological-satellite contribution to date (EV-EOCONTIN-13) - in the next leaders' statement.

australian_inputs.title: Sovereign launch and reconstitution pathway
australian_inputs.description: The stated ambition for a resilient, reconstitutable architecture is not matched by a funded sovereign launch pathway: the 2024 NDS/IIP omitted national launch, while Gilmour's Eris flew a 14-second maiden test in July 2025 and the US TSA (in force July 2024) enables US launches from Australia.
australian_inputs.authority: Defence Space Strategy 2022 (reconstitution objective); ASA civil priority 'access to space'
australian_inputs.success_condition: A credible sovereign or assured-access reconstitution option exists for priority payloads.

leverage_points.why: The Technology Safeguards Agreement provides the legal framework for US launches from Australian territory - the enabling instrument for any responsive-launch and reconstitution pathway (entered into force 23 July 2024 per EV-USSFFORC-15).
leverage_points.next_action: Broker a first US commercial launch campaign under TSA conditions with a parallel Defence position on responsive-launch access (EV-USSFFORC-15).

leverage_points.why: The UK-Australia Space Bridge is the standing civil framework through which launch and space-industry collaboration with the UK is channelled.
leverage_points.next_action: Add a launch-collaboration annex covering UK payload demand for Australian spaceports (vehicle in force since February 2021).

leverage_points.why: The Space MAITRI launch agreement is Australia's only contracted launch line with India and a template for follow-on access to Indian launch capacity.
leverage_points.next_action: Hold the MAITRI launch slot (reported NET 2027, unscheduled as of March 2026 - EV-INDIACOC-10, TO_VERIFY) and scope a follow-on launch option with NSIL.

australian_inputs.title: Space control to deny interference or attack
australian_inputs.description: The 2024 IIP commits to measures enhancing Defence's space control capability to deny attempts to interfere with, or attack, Australia's use of the space domain.
australian_inputs.authority: 2024 Integrated Investment Program; 2024 National Defence Strategy
australian_inputs.success_condition: Australia contributes meaningfully to allied space-control operations and can protect its own use of space.

leverage_points.why: MNF Operation Olympic Defender is the standing multinational vehicle through which Australia exercises its funded space-control commitment (Operation Dyurra contribution).
leverage_points.next_action: Define the Australian input to the MNF-OOD "defence of orbital assets" concept of operations expected complete by end-2026, building on the spring 2026 Operation Selene serial (EV-MULTILAT-19).

leverage_points.why: The CSpO Principals' Board directed a redoubling of capability delivery in support of MNF-OOD at its 17 April 2026 meeting.
leverage_points.next_action: Table an expanded Australian sensor-and-personnel offer at the next Principals' Board (cadence evidenced: 2-4 December 2025 Toulouse, 17 April 2026 Colorado Springs - EV-MULTILAT-12, EV-MULTILAT-13).

leverage_points.why: Schriever Wargame is the coalition venue where space-control concepts are stress-tested; August 2025 was the last iteration planned unilaterally.
leverage_points.next_action: Secure Australian planning roles in the first co-planned Schriever iteration after the August 2025 wargame (EV-MULTILAT-17).

leverage_points.why: The 2023 USSPACECOM-Defence Space Command Enhanced Space Cooperation MoU is the bilateral instrument beneath operational space-control cooperation.
leverage_points.next_action: Scope a space-control annex consistent with the June 2026 Statement of Intent on military space operations (EV-USSFFORC-12).

australian_inputs.title: Defence space workforce build
australian_inputs.description: The DSR 2023 called for a method to build and sustain a trained Defence space workforce; the first ADF members completed dedicated space operations officer and specialist courses only in June 2026.
australian_inputs.success_condition: A sustained space workforce pipeline exists across operations, capability and intelligence roles.

leverage_points.why: The Enhanced Space Cooperation MoU underpins Australian embeds and liaison posts in USSF/USSPACECOM - the fastest workforce maturation channel (an Australian O-6 is deputy commander of US Space Forces Indo-Pacific, EV-USSFFORC-11).
leverage_points.next_action: Expand embed and exchange billets following the inaugural ADF Space Initial Employment Training graduation of June 2026 (EV-USSFFORC-12).

leverage_points.why: The Joint Commercial Operations construct gives Australian operators a qualification pipeline: the 1SSU Commercial Data Mission Centre delivered Australia's first international JCO-200 course in September 2025.
leverage_points.next_action: Schedule the next JCO-200 course serial at the Adelaide CDMC and open seats to partner personnel (EV-JAPANSDA-16, EV-JAPANSDA-17).

leverage_points.why: The Japan 2+2 mandated space dialogues and unit-level exchanges (5 September 2025), and reciprocal operations-command liaison exchanges are commencing.
leverage_points.next_action: Convert the commencing liaison-officer exchange (EV-JAPANSDA-02) into a standing reciprocal space-unit exchange line at the next 2+2 (12th held 5 September 2025).

leverage_points.why: Global Sentinel is the widest multinational SDA exercise available to Australian operators for repetitions alongside 30 nations.
leverage_points.next_action: Bid additional Australian analyst seats for the next Global Sentinel after GS25 (28 April - 9 May 2025, EV-MULTILAT-16).

australian_inputs.title: National space policy unifying civil and security settings
australian_inputs.description: Space intersects more than 25 government portfolios yet Australia lacks a national space policy; the ASA Advisory Board was dissolved in early 2026 and whole-of-government strategy development was reported on hold in 2024.
australian_inputs.authority: USSC brief recommendation 3 (open-source); DSR 2023 centralisation direction
australian_inputs.success_condition: A single national policy links civil priorities, Defence space investment and partnership settings.

leverage_points.why: The ASA-US civil SSA Statement of Intent is a live test of whether Australian civil and security space settings can be worked coherently with one partner.
leverage_points.next_action: Confirm the TraCSS pathway under US funding uncertainty (EV-USSCSPAC-17) and record the civil-defence interface lessons for the national policy case.

leverage_points.why: The Quad space working group is the venue where Australia's civil space commitments meet those of security partners - exposing the cost of the missing national policy.
leverage_points.next_action: Consolidate a single Australian civil-security space position for the next Quad cycle (11th Foreign Ministers' Meeting held 26 May 2026, EV-PACIFICC-17).

leverage_points.why: COPUOS membership carries Australia's norms and space-traffic positions; a unified national policy would strengthen the mandate.
leverage_points.next_action: Align COPUOS positions with the SSA/space-traffic priorities in the ASA-OSC SoI (EV-USSCSPAC-16).

australian_inputs.title: USSF Force Design integration window (IPS LOE 1, 2025-26)
australian_inputs.description: The USSF International Partnership Strategy invites allies into Force Design from the start - common baseline taxonomy and interoperability requirements for the objective force - a task open now on a 5-15 year design horizon, with Australia holding named equities and an allied-officer channel.
australian_inputs.success_condition: Australian requirements are embedded in USSF objective-force taxonomy and capability area designs.

leverage_points.why: The 3 June 2026 USSF-Australian Space Command Statement of Intent is the direct instrument for the Force Design window - service-chief signatures on deepening military space operations cooperation.
leverage_points.next_action: Commit named Australian planners against The Objective Force 2040 baseline (released 15 April 2026) through the SF/S9 staff group established 21 April 2026 (EV-USSFFORC-06, EV-USSFFORC-07, EV-USSFFORC-12).

leverage_points.why: The Enhanced Space Cooperation MoU (2023) is the standing command-level instrument beneath the SoI for staff talks and planner access.
leverage_points.next_action: Add a force-design coordination annex reflecting the IPS LOE 1 tasks reassigned to SF/S9 after Space Futures Command was not activated (EV-USSFFORC-05, EV-USSFFORC-10).

leverage_points.why: The Enhanced Space Cooperation force posture initiative anchors the physical/hosting dimension of force-design integration on Australian territory.
leverage_points.next_action: Map Australian hosting equities (DARC, SST, C-band) into objective-force architecture submissions (EV-USSFFORC-17, EV-USSFFORC-18).

leverage_points.why: CSpO is the multilateral hedge: force-design alignment briefed through CSpO keeps other allies interoperable with the same baseline.
leverage_points.next_action: Brief Australian force-design participation at the next CSpO Principals' Board (last met 17 April 2026 - EV-MULTILAT-13).

australian_inputs.title: Southern-hemisphere geography and ground-segment hosting as the national value proposition
australian_inputs.description: Australia's geography, low population density and landscape diversity underpin allied SDA sensing (Exmouth concentration), EO calibration/validation, TT&C hosting (Cocos for ISRO) and launch/return access - the most credible near-term alliance offering.
australian_inputs.authority: Open-source assessments (USSC 2026; corroborated sensor basing facts)
australian_inputs.success_condition: Ground-segment hosting is priced, governed and reciprocated as a deliberate national offer.

leverage_points.why: The Cocos (Keeling) TT&C terminal - commissioned under ISRO contract with Nova Systems as project manager - is the operating proof that Australian geography converts to partnership currency.
leverage_points.next_action: Sustain tracking support through the Gaganyaan uncrewed G1 mission (officially likely H2 2026, with reported slip risk to Q3 2027 - EV-INDIACOC-14, EV-INDIACOC-15) and price the follow-on as an enduring hosted service.

leverage_points.why: The TSA converts Australian launch/return geography into a usable US market offering - the second pillar of the geography value proposition.
leverage_points.next_action: Land a first TSA-governed launch campaign to give the geography offer a commercial precedent (EV-USSFFORC-15).

leverage_points.why: DARC hosting extends the geography proposition into deep-space sensing - the third pillar, already delivering.
leverage_points.next_action: Document hosting terms and offsets as a reusable national template before DARC full operations expected 2027 (EV-SDAPROGR-09).

leverage_points.why: The JAXA-ASA MoC carries ground-segment and sample-return heritage (Woomera) that can be repeated for Japanese missions.
leverage_points.next_action: Offer TT&C/ground-segment hosting for Japan's FY2026 SDA satellite programme under the MoC (EV-JAPANSDA-13).

australian_inputs.title: Civil SSA and space traffic cooperation
australian_inputs.description: The ASA-US Office of Space Commerce Joint SoI (17 Oct 2024) covers re-entry monitoring and prediction referencing TraCSS and the Civil Space Monitoring Pathfinder; debris monitoring is a national civil priority area.
australian_inputs.authority: ASA-OSC Joint Statement of Intent (17 Oct 2024); ASA civil priority areas
australian_inputs.success_condition: Operational civil SSA data exchange with partners survives US program funding uncertainty.

leverage_points.why: The ASA-Office of Space Commerce Statement of Intent (17 October 2024) is the operating civil SSA instrument, exposed to US TraCSS funding uncertainty.
leverage_points.next_action: Confirm the TraCSS data pathway and agree a fallback exchange mode given reported US funding cuts (EV-USSCSPAC-16, EV-USSCSPAC-17).

leverage_points.why: COPUOS is the standing multilateral venue for space-traffic and debris norms where civil SSA cooperation is legitimised.
leverage_points.next_action: Align Australian debris-monitoring positions with the ASA-OSC SoI work programme (EV-USSCSPAC-16).

leverage_points.why: JCO's commercial-unclassified construct is the practical bridge between civil SSA data and defence SDA operations.
leverage_points.next_action: Verify the JCO participation instrument (vehicle TO_VERIFY) and route civil-usable commercial SSA products through the Adelaide CDMC (EV-JAPANSDA-16).

australian_inputs.title: Export-control geometry: AUKUS licence-free versus permits for all other partners
australian_inputs.description: Most DSGL space technology moves permit-free among AU/UK/US, while equivalent collaboration with Japan, India, ESA states and commercial customers still requires DEC permits (reg 13E, s10, s10A, s10C) - a structural asymmetry shaping every non-AUKUS space partnership.
australian_inputs.authority: Defence Trade Controls Amendment Act 2024; DSGL 2024
australian_inputs.success_condition: Permit pathways and country-list settings match partnership ambitions without compliance surprises.

leverage_points.why: The AUKUS licence-free environment is the favourable side of the export-control geometry - most DSGL space technology moves permit-free among AU/UK/US.
leverage_points.next_action: Publish internal guidance mapping which space collaboration lines qualify licence-free versus permit-required (EV-DECDSGL-21, EV-AUKUSLFE-14).

leverage_points.why: The Defense Trade Cooperation Treaty remains the treaty-level US channel for controlled-technology movement outside the AUKUS exemption categories.
leverage_points.next_action: Route MTCR-excluded items (launch-vehicle technology remains excluded from the AUKUS exemption) through DTCT/individual-licence planning (EV-AUKUSLFE-05).

leverage_points.why: The July 2026 Australia-India PACTS partnership is the newest venue to streamline critical-technology and supply-chain settings with a permit-required partner.
leverage_points.next_action: Use the PACTS work programme (in force July 2026) to pre-clear the permit pathway for Space MAITRI follow-on hardware (EV-DECDSGL-21, EV-INDIACOC-08).

leverage_points.why: The 2014 Defence Equipment and Technology Transfer Agreement is the standing legal basis for controlled space-technology movement with Japan.
leverage_points.next_action: Confirm the agreement covers planned SDA data-system and QZSS ground-segment collaboration, and sequence DEC permits early (EV-DECDSGL-22).

australian_inputs.title: Pacific space-enabled connectivity and resilience assistance
australian_inputs.description: Pacific states dependent on single submarine cables are adopting LEO satellite services amid strategic competition; the Boe Declaration and 2050 Strategy give Australia a Pacific-endorsed frame for space-enabled connectivity and MDA assistance.
australian_inputs.authority: Boe Declaration 2018; 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent; Australian CCRC funding
australian_inputs.success_condition: Australian-supported connectivity and space-enabled services are adopted through Pacific-led mechanisms.

leverage_points.why: IPMDA is the operating Quad arrangement that already delivers commercial satellite RF data to Pacific partners - the established channel for space-enabled assistance.
leverage_points.next_action: Extend the satellite RF data provision recommitted at the 10th and 11th Quad Foreign Ministers' Meetings (1 July 2025; 26 May 2026 - EV-PACIFICC-16, EV-PACIFICC-17) into the Pacific tier Australia carries (EV-PACIFICC-21).

leverage_points.why: The Pacific Fusion Centre is the Boe Declaration institution through which IPMDA Pacific delivery is routed - the partner-accepted insertion point for space-derived data.
leverage_points.next_action: Formalise a space-derived MDA data feed to the Pacific Fusion Centre alongside the FFA channel (EV-PACIFICC-14, EV-PACIFICC-15).

leverage_points.why: The Boe Declaration's expanded security concept is the Pacific-endorsed frame that keeps connectivity and MDA assistance from reading as an external security agenda.
leverage_points.next_action: Badge all space-enabled connectivity assistance to Boe/2050 Strategy priorities (EV-PACIFIC-21).

leverage_points.why: PIF membership and the Lagatoi Declaration digital agenda give the regional forum route for LEO-connectivity resilience standards and gateway models.
leverage_points.next_action: Advance the community-gateway resilience model (Nauru December 2024; Kosrae February 2025 precedents - EV-PACIFICC-05) through the PIF ICT ministerial track (Lagatoi Declaration, EV-PACIFICC-19).

australian_inputs.title: Resourcing execution risk: domestic approval gap and US appropriations exposure
australian_inputs.description: Domestically, ASPI's reading of the 2024 IIP is that only ~$590m of the $9-12bn planned space investment was actually approved through 2034 (EV-AUINPUTS-09, TO_VERIFY) against a strategy conceding it lacks the what/how/when of execution (EV-AUINPUTS-06); analyst commentary reports DARC support costs pressuring JP9360 (EV-AUINPUTS-14, Low). On the partner side, TraCSS faces funding cuts (EV-USSCSPAC-17) and Landsat Next is uncertain in US budget debates despite Australia's commitment (EV-USSCSPAC-19). Carried from the register 2026-07-18; the model's time_resources scores citing the IIP envelope now carry the planned-vs-approved caveat.
australian_inputs.authority: 2024 IIP (funding envelopes); approved-funding figure unconfirmed in the register
australian_inputs.success_condition: Custodian-verified reconciliation of approved vs planned space funding against the 2026 IIP; US-exposed programs covered by fallback arrangements or documented risk acceptance.

leverage_points.why: AUSMIN is where US-exposed program terms are re-baselined when US budgets restructure (DEP-10 treatment).
leverage_points.next_action: Table re-baselined terms for US-exposed programs (Landsat Next first, GL-33) at the next AUSMIN (last held 8 December 2025).
leverage_points.timing: next AUSMIN (not yet scheduled as of 18 Jul 2026)

australian_inputs.title: Continuity of space-enabled critical national functions
australian_inputs.description: Subsea cables, landing stations, space links and the private networks that run them are vital functions to harden against hybrid disruption, with planned national workarounds if they fail (EV-TOTALDEF-08, Army-sponsored research, not policy; transferable-mechanisms assessment EV-TOTALDEF-21). The SLACIP Act 2022 already includes space technology among eleven critical infrastructure sectors (EV-CONVERSA-13). Carried from the register 2026-07-18: no evidence of exercised continuity plans for space-service failure exists in the register.
australian_inputs.authority: SLACIP Act 2022; AARC OP39 is indicative Army-sponsored thinking only (EV-TOTALDEF-20)
australian_inputs.success_condition: Space-enabled vital functions mapped with exercised continuity plans per service class (PNT, SATCOM, EO/weather); priority space-service agreements upgraded from goodwill/commercial terms to defined availability and crisis-priority clauses.

leverage_points.why: The WGS MoU's assured-access model is the register's exemplar of a priority-access arrangement - the contractual form goodwill space services need (SCN-02).
leverage_points.next_action: Upgrade goodwill space-service arrangements to priority-access/availability terms, starting with the OPP-14 availability contract and OPP-20 DAP renewal clause sets (V7 s53/s54).
leverage_points.timing: with OPP-14 contract and OPP-20 DAP renewal

australian_inputs.title: Sovereign R&D, industrial base and cal/val niche as partnership currency
australian_inputs.description: Offer-side assets evidenced in the register: DSTG Quantum-Assured PNT and Resilient Multi-Mission Space STaR Shots (EV-AUINPUTS-16); a $4.6bn/~17,000-FTE space sector with nine Australian satellites launched in 2024 (EV-CONVERSA-16); EO calibration/validation niche (EV-USSCSPAC-03); USSC recommendations to recognise sovereign assets for burden-sharing (EV-USSCSPAC-06, EV-USSCSPAC-07). January 2026 Space Machines Company award TO_VERIFY (EV-USSCSPAC-20). Carried from the register 2026-07-18: without the offer side, dependency-driven partnerships negotiate from weakness.

leverage_points.why: The AUKUS licence-free environment carries the sovereign quantum-PNT line (QuantX clocks contracted 2024 expressly as enabling AUKUS partners' PNT development) - offer-side currency in tradeable form.
leverage_points.next_action: Structure the TEMPO.Space clock demonstration and one cal/val service as priced Australian offsets in the next US/AUKUS negotiation round (EV-RESILIEN-14, EV-USSCSPAC-03).

instruments.name: ANZUS Treaty (Security Treaty between Australia, New Zealand and the United States)
instruments.scope: Mutual security treaty: parties consult on Pacific threats and act to meet common danger per constitutional processes. US-NZ leg suspended since 1986; Australia-US leg fully active.
instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Signed 1 September 1951 in San Francisco; entered into force 29 April 1952 and remains in force indefinitely. Independently verified via the National Museum of Australia (nma.gov.au/defining-moments/resources/anzus-treaty) and Britannica, not the cited Avalon Project. Caveat: US-NZ security obligations under the treaty have been suspended since 1986, but the Australia-US leg — the relevant one for this bilateral list — is fully operative as of mid-2026 (reaffirmed at AUSMIN, December 2025).

instruments.name: AUSMIN (Australia-United States Ministerial Consultations)
instruments.scope: Principal 2+2 foreign/defence ministers forum setting alliance direction; source of most new bilateral initiatives.
instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: First AUSMIN held in Canberra in 1985 (Shultz/Hayden/Beazley era) and held most years since — verified via DFAT (dfat.gov.au/geo/united-states-of-america/ausmin) and the US Studies Centre 'A brief history of AUSMIN', independent of the cited state.gov page. Mid-2026 status: active — the most recent AUSMIN was held 8 December 2025 in Washington DC (Rubio/Hegseth hosting Wong/Marles), explicitly marking 40 years of the forum; also covered by Australian Defence Ministers media release of 7 December 2025 and a Feb 2026 CRS report (R48875).

instruments.name: Force Posture Agreement (FPA) 2014
instruments.scope: Legally binding framework for US force posture initiatives in Australia; 25-year term, terminable on one year's notice. Umbrella for MRF-D, Enhanced Air Cooperation and Enhanced Space Cooperation.
instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Signed in Sydney on 12 August 2014 by Bishop/Johnston (Australia) and Kerry/Hagel (US) — verified via the treaty text and National Interest Analysis on AustLII and aph.gov.au, not the cited Defence page. It entered into force in 2015 (registered as [2015] ATS 1 in the Australian Treaty Series) and remains in force as of mid-2026: the 2023 AUSMIN force posture initiatives (including Enhanced Space Cooperation) are expressly conducted under this Agreement, and force posture cooperation featured again at AUSMIN December 2025.

instruments.name: Enhanced Space Cooperation (US Force Posture Initiative)
instruments.scope: Space-domain stream of the US Force Posture Initiatives under the FPA umbrella (listed by Defence alongside MRF-D and EAC).

verification.note: The vehicle exists under exactly this name and the cited defence.gov.au page is real, but the 'date unknown' field can be filled: the AUSMIN 2023 Joint Statement (Brisbane, 29 July 2023 — minister.defence.gov.au/statements/2023-07-29/... and 2021-2025.state.gov joint statement) records the principals declaring 'Enhanced Space Cooperation as a new Force Posture Initiative', operating under the 2014 Force Posture Agreement. verification.note: All named elements independently verified: HyFliTE Project Arrangement signed ~18-19 November 2024 (defence.gov.au; DefenseScoop) with first hypersonic test flight noted at AUKMIN June 2026; first Pillar II Signature Project — payloads and enabling systems for uncrewed undersea vehicles — announced 30 May 2026 at the AUKUS Defence Ministers' Meeting (GOV.UK fact sheet; first capabilities from 2027); AUKUS-designed AI algorithms deployed on an Australian P-8A; REPMUS (Portugal) participation under the Maritime Big Play autonomy programme. Date fill-in: Pillar II (Advanced Capabilities) dates from the original AUKUS announcement of September 2021. It is a programme of work, not a treaty, so 'in force' should read 'active/ongoing' — which it is as of mid-2026.

instruments.name: Agreement between Australia and the UK for Defence and Security Cooperation (2024 modernised DCA)

instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Existence and date confirmed from the treaty text itself: 'DONE at Canberra, on this Twenty-first day of March 2024', signed by Grant Shapps and Richard Marles (UK command paper CP 1256, CS Australia No.1/2025). Status resolved: signed but not yet in force per available public record as of 18 July 2026. The command paper (Jan 2025) states '[The Agreement is not in force]'; Article 14(1) provides it 'replaces the 2014 DSC Treaty' and enters into force on the last written notification; UK CRaG scrutiny concluded early March 2025; Australia's JSCOT inquiry lapsed at the 28 March 2025 dissolution and the re-constituted JSCOT backed ratification in Report 228 (Oct 2025); no entry-into-force announcement or ATS registration was found. Residual uncertainty: entry into force via exchange of notes could occur without prominent publicity.

instruments.name: Australia-Germany annual senior officials' strategic dialogues (Indo-Pacific, National Security, Defence, bilateral) under the ESP

instruments.name: Australia-Germany Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA)
instruments.scope: Would formalise legal status, access and ease of operation for each other's forces (per Marles: make it 'much easier for our defense forces to operate from each other's countries'); linked to commitments to facilitate movement of defence personnel and equipment through respective territories.
instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: The June 2026 2+2 joint statement (BMVG-hosted PDF, independent of the cited URL) states: 'Following agreement in April 2026 to pursue a status of forces agreement, today Ministers announced the formal commencement of negotiations towards, and shared commitment to, reaching in-principle agreement of the text by the end of 2026.' The intent to pursue a SOFA was first publicly announced by Marles and Pistorius in Canberra on 26 March 2026 (Bloomberg; The New Daily). So as of mid-July 2026 the treaty is under negotiation and unsigned — 'date unknown, under negotiation' is exactly right. Minor timeline nuance: the official statement dates the agreement-to-pursue to April 2026, while press coverage of the announcement is 26 March 2026.

instruments.name: Exchange of Notes constituting an Agreement between Australia and the Federal Republic of Germany for the Reciprocal Safeguarding of Classified Material [1979] ATS 20
instruments.scope: Mutual protection of exchanged classified material at equivalent national classification levels; no third-state release or purpose-change without originator consent; security-cleared visit access regime. The operative bilateral information-security instrument.
instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Existence and citation confirmed via Wikipedia's 'Australia-Germany bilateral treaties' list (exact title, ATS 20 of 1979) and the AustLII Australian Treaties Library index; the constituting Note Verbale is dated 27 November 1979, matching the 1979-11 date. In-force status supported by Australia's AGSVA Defence Security of Information Agreements fact sheet (agsva.gov.au, April 2024), which lists Germany among countries holding a current SIA with industrial provisions, and no evidence of termination or replacement was found. Caveat: the AGSVA fact sheet does not name the 1979 instrument specifically, and the AustLII treaty page itself was Cloudflare-blocked, so entry-into-force particulars rest on the ATS citation and secondary confirmation.

Name (DOI/arrangement), date (2026-03), and status all check out.

instruments.scope: Legal framework for the bilateral defence relationship; understood to underpin ADF presence/HQ establishment in the UAE and the joint defence committee process.

verification.note: Verified against the primary treaty text PDF downloaded from aph.gov.au (JSCT 17 June 2008 tabled treaties): cover page reads "[2007] ATNIF 10" and testimonium reads "Done at Abu Dhabi, on this twenty-third day of April 2007". verification.correction: Signed at Abu Dhabi on 23 April 2007 (not 2008); official text title is "Agreement between the Government of Australia and the Government of the United Arab Emirates concerning Defence Cooperation" [2007] ATNIF 10. 2008 is the year of JSCT review/ratification steps, not signature.

instruments.name: Al Minhad Air Base access / Camp Baird (ADF host-nation basing arrangement)
instruments.scope: Host-nation access to Al Minhad AB near Dubai (ADF precinct 'Camp Baird'): HQ Joint Task Force 633 / HQ Middle East and reception-staging hub for the Middle East Area of Operations; supported Operations Slipper (2001-14), Accordion (2014- ), Manitou, Okra and Highroad.

verification.note: Confirmed via sources independent of the cited Defence article. Nautilus Institute: ADF first used Al Minhad in 2003 (RAAF AP-3C Orions); the ADF Middle East Area of Operations command shifted from Baghdad to Al Minhad in late 2008 (matching the claimed 2008 date); facilities renamed Camp Baird in February 2014 after Cpl Cameron Baird VC MG; the governing host-nation/SOFA-type arrangement is deliberately non-public (its existence is not officially acknowledged, so no public instrument date exists). Mid-2026 status: arrangement still operating — Defence's official statement of 18 March 2026 on Iranian strikes on Al Minhad confirms the ADF's "long-standing presence"; the base was struck again in a May 2026 Iranian wave (The Nightly, Wikipedia's 2026 Iranian strikes on the UAE), with ADF personnel (~70-80, HQ Middle East supporting up to 12 operations) safe and no withdrawal reported as of July 2026. Caveat: 2008 is the HQ-relocation year; ADF use began 2003. Sources: https://nautilus.org/publications/books/australian-forces-abroad/australian-bases-abroad/mirage/; https://www.defence.gov.au/news-events/releases/2026-03-18/statement-strikes-al-minhad-air-base; https://thenightly.com.au/world/iran-strikes-al-minhad-base-home-to-australian-forces-for-second-time-c-21981584

verification.note: Existence and date confirmed via sources other than the cited page: signed 14 February 2019 at Lot Fourteen, Adelaide — the Australian Space Agency's fourth international MoU — covering a framework for collaboration in civil space, information/technology/personnel exchange. Corroborated by the Department of Industry (industry.gov.au news and hosted MoU PDF, dated 2019-04), SpaceWatch.Global (Feb 2019, "Australia And UAE Space Agencies Sign Partnership MoU In Adelaide") and space.gov.au's news item. On the TO_VERIFY status: mid-2026 operational status could not be authoritatively established — it is a non-binding MoU, no public renewal or termination announcement was found, and it remains published among ASA's international arrangements (space.gov.au pages were listed in search indexes but timed out on fetch; the industry.gov.au PDF is bot-blocked, so any expiry clause could not be read). instruments.name: Artemis Accords (multilateral - Australia and UAE both signatories)
instruments.scope: Non-binding multilateral principles for civil space exploration. instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Confirmed via sources independent of the cited space.gov.au page: the Artemis Accords were signed 13 October 2020 by eight founding signatories — Australia, Canada, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, the UAE, the UK and the US — per the US State Department, SpacePolicyOnline, Britannica and NASA's own announcement listing both Australia and the UAE. Both remain signatories and the Accords remain operative in 2026 with substantially expanded membership (NASA "International Partners Deepen Commitment to Artemis Accords"; State Department Artemis Accords page). instruments.name: Papua New Guinea–Australia Mutual Defence Treaty (Pukpuk Treaty)

instruments.label: FACT

verification.note: Signed by PMs Albanese and Marape in October 2025 (DFAT maintains a dedicated treaty page and PDF; Defence Ministers issued a treaty-implementation joint statement dated 2025-10-20). verification.note: Signed San Francisco 1 September 1951; entered into force 29 April 1952; concluded for indefinite duration and never terminated. Independent sources: Avalon Project (avalon.law.yale.edu/20th_century/usmu002.asp), National Museum of Australia (nma.gov.au). Caveat worth recording: the US suspended its treaty obligations to New Zealand in 1986 over NZ's nuclear-free policy, so the US-NZ leg is suspended while the treaty as a whole, and the Australia-US alliance under it, remains in force through mid-2026.
