dependencies.description: United States concentration across every core mission area: WGS wideband access, M-code PNT, DARC/SST/C-band SDA hosting and operation, Landsat Next EO, TraCSS civil SSA, force design and the JCO construct. Australia is assessed as structurally dependent on the US for core space services.
dependencies.treatment: Deliberate diversification per the framework: second-ally legs (Japan OPP-17; Germany Declaration of Intent on a global space-surveillance sensor network, March 2026 - VEH-GERMANY-09), sovereign-tasked commercial layers (OPP-18, OPP-20), and sovereignty conditions (fallback, exit, data control per V7 s53) written into every new US arrangement. CIRCULARITY NOTE (red-team 2026-07-18): OPP-18 and OPP-20 are themselves on this dependency's affected list - they diversify provider/information-domain concentration inside US-anchored constructs, not US-nation concentration; the only non-US diversification legs (OPP-17 Build; OPP-02 P-DE Explore) sit outside tranche 1. Tranche 1 therefore deepens this dependency until governance either records acceptance with a review trigger or pulls a diversification action forward (see plan directive).
dependencies.treatment_owner: TO_ASSIGN (proposed class: Defence Space Command + Strategy, Policy & Industry)

dependencies.description: Japan single-source dependency for geostationary weather imagery: BoM services are critically dependent on JMA's Himawari, with Himawari-10 development delayed and the ALOS-4 SAR access channel unresolved.
dependencies.treatment: Sustain the BoM-JMA Strategic Relationship Arrangement (11 November 2024) with Australian Himawari-10 co-investment; define custodian-confirmed contingency access to alternative imagery at comparable cadence (the input's stated success condition).

dependencies.description: Interim military SATCOM rides on two single hosted payloads and one provider family: Optus C1 (aging, inclined orbit, contracted to September 2034 on 2022-vintage evidence) and Intelsat/SES IS-22 UHF (to at least 2033) - with SES describing limited comparable UHF capacity in the Indo-Pacific.
dependencies.treatment: Deliver the SPA9102 sovereign UHF bird with availability-based support; design the wideband RFT for multi-provider award; hold IS-22 extension options (to 2041) as bridge, not destination.
dependencies.treatment_owner: TO_ASSIGN (proposed class: CASG Air Defence & Space Systems)

dependencies.description: Starlink has become the de facto Pacific disaster-resilience connectivity layer (Vanuatu earthquake response, Tonga restoration) - a single commercial provider under mixed regional governance, with the main alternative (Kacific) shrinking its satellite ambitions.
dependencies.treatment: Promote the in-country community-gateway model (Nauru, Kosrae precedents), multi-vendor LEO procurement guidance through the CCRC research line, and cable redundancy (Tu'i Vava'u model) so no Pacific partner depends on one provider's policy.

dependencies.description: Legacy single-orbit GEO concentration in military SATCOM persists until the multi-orbit architecture is delivered: the JP9102 cancellation rationale itself, with the first multi-orbit elements (sovereign LEO demonstrator) not due until early 2028.
dependencies.treatment: Hold the NDS/IIP multi-orbit commitment through Second Pass; scope the alternative-space-communications line of effort; sequence the Optus/Inovor LEO demonstration (early 2028) as the proof point.
dependencies.treatment_owner: TO_ASSIGN (proposed class: CASG Air Defence & Space Systems)

dependencies.description: Operational SDA and warning depend on allied-classified feeds: DARC Early Use is conducted remotely by the US 20th Space Surveillance Squadron, Australian data-access terms are unconfirmed, and the sovereign fusion layer (JP9360) shows no contract award in 2025-26.
dependencies.treatment: Secure DARC data-access terms before 2027 full operations; fund the sovereign JP9360 layer; grow the commercial-unclassified JCO tier as the releasable hedge; work CSpO information-sharing barriers through the PLWG line Australia hosted in June 2025. (Data-access precondition now tracked as GL-31 with owner class and pre-2027-FOC due date.)

dependencies.description: All Australian PNT rests on foreign-owned GNSS; SouthPAN - the flagship national augmentation - itself relies on GPS data as essential input, procures its space segment from a foreign operator, and excludes northern Australia from planned Safety-of-Life coverage.
dependencies.treatment: Layered mitigation per the ADF multi-layered PNT approach: M-code access, sovereign quantum timing (TEMPO.Space), LEO-PNT evaluation, and the ANCHOR-recommended national PNT policy (none exists as of February 2026).
dependencies.treatment_owner: TO_ASSIGN (proposed class: Joint PNT Directorate / JCG)

dependencies.description: National SDA sensing is concentrated on one peninsula: the SST, C-band radar and DARC Site 1 all sit at or beside Harold E. Holt, Exmouth - a single geographic point of failure for weather, attack or accident.
dependencies.treatment: Geographic dispersal through the commercial layer (LeoLabs south-west WA radar, EOS Mount Stromlo/Learmonth, Silentium Swan Reach SA) and reliance on DARC Sites 2-3 (UK 2030, third US site) for global redundancy.

dependencies.description: Every opportunity in the portfolio draws on a nascent space workforce: first ADF Space Initial Employment Training graduates June 2026, the Joint PNT Directorate is ~17 people, and the DSR-directed workforce method is not evidenced as established.
dependencies.treatment: Partner training pipelines as the fastest levers: JCO-200 course line, reciprocal Japan exchanges, US embeds and command billets, exercise repetitions (OPP-21); sequence new commitments against workforce reality rather than ambition.

dependencies.description: US appropriations exposure across programs Australia has bought into: Landsat Next restructured/descoped in the FY2026 request after Australia committed A$207.4m+, TraCSS faces funding cuts, and the SDA Transport Layer/MILNET line has changed direction twice in one budget cycle.; domestically, ASPI's reading of the 2024 IIP is that only ~$590m of the $9-12bn planned space investment was approved through 2034 (EV-AUINPUTS-09, TO_VERIFY) - the two-sided resourcing execution risk carried as AUS-IN-13
dependencies.treatment: Fallback arrangements and documented risk acceptance for each US-exposed program; diversified channels (Copernicus hub, Japan legs, commercial EO) held at readiness; partnership terms re-baselined at AUSMIN when US programs restructure.
dependencies.treatment_owner: TO_ASSIGN (proposed class: Defence Strategy, Policy & Industry + DFAT)

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: Under normalised grey-zone counterspace activity (jamming, dazzling, cyber intrusion, co-orbital manoeuvre), does the portfolio still deliver its effects?

portfolio_impact.impact: Jamming pressure validates the multi-orbit case and raises the value of assured-access annexes.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Interim posture (WGS + C1 + IS-22) with EMI-resilient narrowband prioritised.

portfolio_impact.impact: EMI/jamming resilience is already an explicit SPA9102 requirement - competition confirms the design brief.
portfolio_impact.fallback: IS-22 anti-jam UHF continuity to 2033+.

portfolio_impact.impact: Attribution demand rises; allied sensor integration becomes daily business rather than contingency.
portfolio_impact.fallback: CSpO shareable tiers if bilateral feeds tighten.

portfolio_impact.impact: Commercial-unclassified SDA becomes the attribution layer that can be shown publicly.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Direct provider contracts outside the JCO construct.

portfolio_impact.impact: MNF-OOD is the standing response vehicle; Operation Selene-type serials become persistent.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Bilateral US channel via the ESC MoU.

portfolio_impact.impact: Jamming/spoofing of GNSS is the demonstrated, currently-employed vector this option answers.
portfolio_impact.fallback: SouthPAN integrity layer for benign-environment functions only.

portfolio_impact.impact: Shareable-tier SDA exchange with Japan builds regional attribution credibility at low cost.
portfolio_impact.fallback: CSpO-track sharing.

scenarios.assessment: The portfolio is broadly competition-shaped: its strongest options (OPP-14, OPP-18, OPP-09) are precisely the grey-zone answers. The binding constraints are workforce depth (DEP-09) and the unfunded sovereign SDA fusion layer (DEP-06), not partner willingness.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: In a regional crisis with concurrent demand, when partners' space assets are committed to their own needs, which Australian services fail first?

portfolio_impact.impact: Civil EO/weather requests may be deprioritised - the Black Summer precedent (a partner declined a data request during its own disaster).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Commercial tasking (OPP-20) plus Copernicus hub products.

portfolio_impact.impact: WGS bandwidth prioritisation risk under US operational demand.
portfolio_impact.fallback: C1/IS-22 hosted capacity and commercial multi-orbit leases.

portfolio_impact.impact: Direct-tasking DAP line is the designed crisis hedge - but only if crisis-priority clauses are contracted.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Multi-vendor spot tasking at surge prices.

portfolio_impact.impact: Pacific RF-data continuity matters most exactly when crisis hits; commercial provider terms decide availability.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Direct DFAT-FFA contract escalation.

portfolio_impact.impact: Starlink surge deployment is proven (300+ units into Vanuatu after the December 2024 earthquake) but rests on one provider's posture.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Community gateways and cable redundancy.

portfolio_impact.impact: QZSS regional augmentation continuity depends on Japanese national priorities.
portfolio_impact.fallback: SouthPAN and GPS civil layers.

portfolio_impact.impact: Cocos support commitments are contractually anchored and low-exposure - a stabiliser.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Reschedule against Gaganyaan slips.

scenarios.assessment: Concurrent-demand denial is the documented, repeated failure mode (Black Summer data refusal; April 2023 Inmarsat outage hitting four states' agriculture). The portfolio answer is contractual: crisis-priority and availability clauses (OPP-14 support model, OPP-20 DAP renewal) convert goodwill services into assured ones. Register input AUS-IN-16 (continuity of space-enabled critical national functions - subsea cables, landing stations, space links) is carried into the model as of 2026-07-18: its success condition - goodwill space-service arrangements upgraded to priority-access agreements - is this scenario's contractual treatment, and OPP-14/OPP-20 commercial legs count as mitigation only once those clauses are contracted.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: In high-intensity conflict with sustained GNSS denial and attacks on SATCOM, which options carry the force?

portfolio_impact.impact: M-code becomes the core navigation-warfare layer; accession status is therefore a war-readiness question, not a program nicety.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Quantum timing + inertial layers under DSTG lines.

portfolio_impact.impact: The EMI-resilient sovereign UHF bird is the survivable C2 backbone for deployed forces.
portfolio_impact.fallback: WGS/MUOS allied capacity under wartime prioritisation.

portfolio_impact.impact: Multi-orbit diversity is the survivability design; single-orbit legacy is the vulnerability the NDS names.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Proliferated-LEO commercial augmentation.

portfolio_impact.impact: MNF-OOD carries the collective space-defence response; the defence-of-orbital-assets CONOPS (due end-2026) is the playbook.
portfolio_impact.fallback: National Op Dyurra tasks under bilateral US C2.

portfolio_impact.impact: DARC deep-space custody feeds targeting-grade awareness of hostile GEO manoeuvre.
portfolio_impact.fallback: SST/C-band plus commercial deep-space telescopes.

portfolio_impact.impact: Force-design integration decides whether Australian systems interoperate under fire in 2030s architectures.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Interface-level interoperability retrofits (costlier, later).

portfolio_impact.impact: GPS-independent commercial PNT moves from experiment to gap-filler if fielded in time.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Terrestrial NAVWAR aids only.

scenarios.assessment: Conflict exposes the difference between access and assurance: every allied service Australia uses will be prioritised by its owner's war needs first (DEP-01). Options that create Australian-controlled capability (OPP-14, OPP-15 quantum line, OPP-18) are the conflict hedges; the rest buy influence over allied prioritisation.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: A partner government restructures, defunds or withdraws from a program Australia has bought into - what breaks?

portfolio_impact.impact: LIVE CASE: the FY2026 US request funds no Landsat Next as designed after Australia committed A$207.4m+; no Australian response yet evidenced.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Copernicus hub, Japan legs, commercial EO (OPP-20).

portfolio_impact.impact: US reorganisation churn is demonstrated (Space Futures Command cancelled before activation; tasks moved to SF/S9).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Institution-agnostic planner relationships; CSpO hedge.

portfolio_impact.impact: PWSA-connection intent is reported but unofficial; a US pivot would strand integration work.
portfolio_impact.fallback: JCO commercial tier and Germany/Japan sensor legs.

portfolio_impact.impact: MGUE accession delay already shows partner-process dependency.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Sovereign quantum line continues regardless.

portfolio_impact.impact: UAE engagement is hostage to third-party (US-UAE) technology politics.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Hold treatment already applied.

portfolio_impact.impact: A Quad-partner pullback would thin IPMDA funding but the FFA delivery channel would survive.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Direct Australian contract with data providers.

portfolio_impact.impact: Indian program slips (Gaganyaan, MAITRI NET 2027) delay but do not cancel the cooperation line.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Stretch timelines; hold grant milestones.

scenarios.assessment: Withdrawal risk is concentrated in Washington (DEP-10) and is not hypothetical - Landsat Next is a live restructure against an Australian nine-figure commitment. The framework treatment (fallback defined before commitment; risk acceptance documented) should be retrofitted to every US-exposed line at the next AUSMIN.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: A commercial provider fails in orbit, exits the market or is acquired by a hostile-influenced owner - what is exposed?

portfolio_impact.impact: Optus C1 is beyond original design life in inclined orbit; the April 2023 Inmarsat I-4 F1 outage is the class precedent.
portfolio_impact.fallback: IS-22 capacity shift and accelerated SPA9102 delivery.

portfolio_impact.impact: Single sovereign GEO bird with ~10-year life concentrates risk at end-of-life - design margin and option satellites matter.
portfolio_impact.fallback: IS-22 extension options to 2041.

portfolio_impact.impact: The commercial SDA base is thin: EOS has already pivoted away from SDA focus; consolidation could remove a layer.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Multi-provider contracts; allied-hosted sensors carry core catalogue.

portfolio_impact.impact: LEO-PNT vendors are pre-revenue; failure is the base case to plan against.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Evaluation-only posture until maturity.

portfolio_impact.impact: Starlink policy change or Kacific failure would strip Pacific resilience overnight (Kacific2 already on hold).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Community gateways + cable redundancy + multi-vendor procurement.

portfolio_impact.impact: Single-vendor DAP concentration; Maxar corporate changes would hit assured access.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Planet-class multi-vendor spread (NSW precedent).

scenarios.assessment: Commercial failure is a demonstrated Australian experience (Inmarsat I-4 F1, 2023), and V7 s54 commercial-mechanism conditions (continuity, data rights, surge, sovereignty) are the standing treatment. Every commercial leg in the v2 portfolio should carry those clauses before it is counted as resilience. (Red-team 2026-07-18: the s54 clause set is now a recorded condition on OPP-14 and OPP-20 mechanism components; DEP treatments carry proposed owner classes pending validation.)

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: Required information cannot be released to Australia (or by Australia to a partner) - which options stall?

portfolio_impact.impact: LIVE CASE: releasability of USSF Force Design artefacts to Australia is the recorded Unknown capping this A-band option.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Work unclassified taxonomy layers; validate release tier via the SoI channel.

portfolio_impact.impact: STANDING RED: MTCR launch-vehicle exclusions from the AUKUS exemption block the highest-scoring option.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Individual US licences; German commercial launch leg.

portfolio_impact.impact: Ten-nation release differentials complicate every multilateral SDA exchange.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Bilateral tiers plus commercial-unclassified layer.

portfolio_impact.impact: Japan sits in CSpO but outside MNF-OOD - release geometry fragments the coalition.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Shareable-tier serials; support US-led evaluation of Japanese membership.

portfolio_impact.impact: Deliberately designed at the shareable tier - resilient to this scenario.
portfolio_impact.fallback: None needed at current scope.

portfolio_impact.impact: Commercial-unclassified JCO tier is the portfolio's systemic mitigation to release denial.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Direct commercial contracts remain open.

portfolio_impact.impact: DEC permit friction with India is the export-control expression of the same problem.
portfolio_impact.fallback: PACTS-track pre-clearance; scope to unclassified payloads.

scenarios.assessment: Release denial is the portfolio's most common binding gap (it caps OPP-07, blocks OPP-08, and shapes OPP-02/09/12). The two structural answers are the commercial-unclassified layer (OPP-18) and shareable-tier design (OPP-04); everything else needs release matrices negotiated case by case.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: A major debris event or launch-failure cascade degrades shared orbital systems - how does the portfolio absorb it?

portfolio_impact.impact: LIVE CASE: QZS-7 postponed by the H3 F8 failure investigation - single-launcher dependency delays the QZSS constellation and its hosted US SDA payload.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Five-satellite QZSS service continues; re-baseline hosting study.

portfolio_impact.impact: Landsat Next's single-vehicle three-satellite design (and its descoped successor) concentrates launch risk; Himawari-10 delay compounds cadence risk.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Cross-constellation layering (Sentinel-2C transition already executed).

portfolio_impact.impact: A Cosmos-1408-class debris event would make the debris-management mission line premium and urgent.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Accelerate MAITRI follow-on scoping with Quad visibility.

portfolio_impact.impact: Catalogue-maintenance demand surges after any fragmentation event - southern-hemisphere sensors become premium capacity.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Commercial radar surge (LeoLabs) purchase.

portfolio_impact.impact: Commercial layer provides surge tracking and NEI characterisation of damaged assets.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Allied tasking priority negotiation.

portfolio_impact.impact: A single GEO UHF bird is exposed to debris risk at one orbital slot - constellation insurance and manoeuvre margin are design requirements.
portfolio_impact.fallback: IS-22 continuity and allied narrowband leases.

portfolio_impact.impact: Exercise scenarios (Apollo Insights TTX series includes proliferated-constellation and nuclear-payload scenarios) rehearse exactly this.
portfolio_impact.fallback: None needed - this is the rehearsal vehicle.

scenarios.assessment: Degradation events are documented (Cosmos 1408: 1,500+ trackable fragments; Fengyun-1C) and the H3 cascade shows launch-failure coupling across programs. SDA options gain value in this scenario; single-bird SATCOM options need explicit debris/manoeuvre design conditions at Second Pass.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: Australian policy resets (a new NDS/IIP cycle, machinery-of-government change, or the long-absent national space policy arriving) - which options survive re-prioritisation?

portfolio_impact.impact: The continuous-capability four-LOE model replaced discrete phases once already; partners must track shifting lines of effort.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Anchor commitments in signed instruments, not program labels.

portfolio_impact.impact: Second Pass is the policy gate; budget pressure (SSN program growth toward $10bn/yr by 2033-34) is the documented competitor.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Descoped narrowband-only delivery with extended IS-22 bridge.

portfolio_impact.impact: JP9360 direction change was flagged by industry at the JP9102 cancellation; tranche funding is exposed each IIP cycle.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Allied-hosted sensors carry the mission (at sovereignty cost).

portfolio_impact.impact: Commercial layer is cheap enough to survive most resets - and is the reconstitution-friendly option.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Maintain minimum-viable contracts.

portfolio_impact.impact: Leader-level elevation (July 2026 Joint Statement) insulates the India line from routine policy churn.
portfolio_impact.fallback: ASA instruments continue under civil settings.

portfolio_impact.impact: Pacific assistance rides aid-budget settings; Boe/2050 framing gives it cross-government durability.
portfolio_impact.fallback: Quad-badged delivery (OPP-19) if bilateral budgets tighten.

scenarios.assessment: Australian policy volatility is documented (JP9102 and NSMEO cancellations, space strategy on hold, ASA advisory board dissolved). Options anchored in signed instruments, leader-level statements or delivered infrastructure survive resets; options resting on program labels do not. The absent national space policy (AUS-IN-06) remains the root fragility.

scenarios.label: ASSESSMENT
scenarios.question: If no recommendation in this pack is approved and the portfolio runs on current settings, what happens? (Do-nothing counterfactual assembled from existing assessments.)

portfolio_impact.impact: The one live acquisition window closes: RFT responses due ~November 2026 pass without a sovereign narrowband decision (EV-MILSATCO-07).
portfolio_impact.fallback: IS-22 extension options to 2041 as bridge - dependency, not capability.

portfolio_impact.impact: Wideband architecture is set by dependency drift rather than deliberate choice as the 2029 WGS access horizon approaches (OPP-01 potential_effect; DEP-01).
portfolio_impact.fallback: WGS + C1 + IS-22 interim posture with no dated decision point before 2029.

portfolio_impact.impact: DARC-vs-JP9360 funding tension resolves itself by default: sustainment continues, the sovereign fusion layer stays unfunded (EV-SDAPROGR-03).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Allied-classified feeds without a sovereign layer (DEP-06 persists).

portfolio_impact.impact: DARC completes to 2027 FOC with Australian data-access terms still unnegotiated - hosting without assured access (EV-SDAPROGR-08).
portfolio_impact.fallback: None recorded - the leverage window closes at FOC.

portfolio_impact.impact: The 2026 Force Design design-in year passes; Australian requirements enter USSF planning by exception, not by design (EV-USSFCSPO-17).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Institution-agnostic planner relationships (SCN-04).

portfolio_impact.impact: Himawari single-source dependency (DEP-02) and the unresolved Landsat restructure persist unmitigated (EV-EOCONTIN-08).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Copernicus/commercial legs at lower cadence, uncontracted for crisis priority.

portfolio_impact.impact: M-code accession remains unconfirmed - a war-readiness gap under GNSS denial, not a program nicety (SCN-03; EV-RESILIEN-09).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Quantum/inertial layers under DSTG lines, unfielded.

portfolio_impact.impact: The commercial SDA layer decays: EOS has pivoted away and no JP9360 money arrives to scale sovereign tasking (EV-SDAPROGR-16, EV-SDAPROGR-03).
portfolio_impact.fallback: Allied-hosted sensors carry the catalogue - deepening DEP-01.
